game: DET @ CAR, Week 4 2026 (kickoff, venue, spread, total not in pack)

script.base: No spread or total is saved, so the lean is inferred from three weeks of form: Detroit is the side more likely to play in front because Jahmyr Gibbs already has 65 carries and 307 rush yards and Carolina has allowed 5.88 yards per carry and 13 runs of 10-plus. Base flow is Detroit handing Gibbs a full early workload, staying run-lean while the lead is comfortable, with Carolina — Damien Lewis out and 0.03 EPA per dropback when blitzed — struggling to stay on schedule and tilting pass if they trail. Pace and garbage-time length are unknown.
script.flip1: Carolina blitzes 37 percent and Detroit's EPA per dropback is 0.48 against the blitz versus 0.13 with no blitz, so Goff may pass Detroit into the lead instead of pounding Gibbs. That is the 52-rush-yard path: Gibbs carries stall, Carolina's leaky middle (12.0 YPA) and 16 allowed passes of 20-plus keep it a shootout, and Hubbard's rushes die while McMillan/Waller/LaPorta volume is the live side.
script.flip2: Ben Bartch is out and Carolina's interior (Cam Jackson and Lee Hunter, both questionable) actually plays, so Gibbs never gets the 156-yard script and finishes under 96.5 in a lower-event game. If that game stays close, Carolina can still grind Chuba Hubbard toward the 82-yard week even with Lewis out.

injury_fallout: Known before kickoff from the nflverse injury report; final inactives (~90 minutes pre-kick) are not in the pack. CAR G Damien Lewis is Out (elbow): Carolina rush efficiency should fall and pressure should rise, which hits Hubbard/Dillon/Brooks rushing and pushes Bryce Young toward quick throws (Hubbard, Waller, Tremble) rather than deep shots. CAR T Monroe Freeling is Questionable (concussion), so the OL hit may be two deep. CAR WR Xavier Legette is Out (knee) after only 6 targets, 64 yards and 97 air yards — a modest redistribution toward Tetairoa McMillan (23 targets), Jalen Coker if active (22 targets, 222 yards), Mitchell Evans, John Metchie III, Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble. CAR WR Jalen Coker is Questionable (quad), not out; if he is inactive that 22-target/252-air role is the real vacancy and those same pass-catchers gain, but that is not assumed. CAR DT Cam Jackson and DT Lee Hunter are Questionable; if both sit, a run defense already at 5.88 YPC gets worse and Gibbs' rush over is stronger. DET G Ben Bartch is Out (foot): Detroit pressure up, rush efficiency down, more quick throws — a direct ding to Gibbs rushing and a small boost to Gibbs/LaPorta/St. Brown short catches. DET CB D.J. Reed is Questionable (rib); if he sits, McMillan sees a backup outside, unconfirmed.

matchup.shell: No coverage charting, man/zone rate, or MOFO/MOFC tag in the pack. Location splits only: Carolina allows 6.65 YPA left (31 att), 6.24 middle (21), 5.52 right (40) — not an explosive pass defense (5 passes of 20-plus, 99 yards). Detroit allows 5.77 left (44), 12.0 middle (22), 8.09 right (57); the middle is the bleed.
matchup.pressure: Carolina blitzes 37 percent; Detroit EPA/dropback is 0.48 vs blitz and 0.13 vs no blitz, so Goff has been much better when pressure is called. Detroit blitzes 35 percent; Carolina EPA/dropback is 0.03 vs blitz and 0.19 vs no blitz, so Young has been worse when Detroit brings pressure. Pressure that gets home should cut Carolina deep yards and lift RB/TE checkdowns.
matchup.bleeds: Carolina's bleed is the run: 5.88 YPC and 13 runs of 10-plus in three games, not the deep pass. Detroit's bleed is explosives and the middle: 16 passes of 20-plus for 135 yards, and 12.0 YPA on 22 middle attempts. Detroit run defense is firmer at 4.61 YPC but has still allowed 12 runs of 10-plus.
matchup.overlap: Detroit's primary ball-carrier, Gibbs (65 of the non-QB carries), attacks the exact place Carolina gives it up (5.88 YPC). Carolina's primary air-yards options, McMillan (295 air yards) and Coker (252, questionable), attack Detroit's explosive/middle bleed, but Detroit's blitz split (Carolina 0.03 EPA vs blitz) cuts against that deep overlap and favors checkdowns instead.

edge_players.must_be_true: Gibbs is healthy and keeps the 20-carry share; Carolina's run defense stays as loose as the three-game split (Jackson/Hunter sitting would help, not required); Bartch's absence does not collapse interior yards per carry; Detroit does not turn this into a pass-only game just because Carolina blitzes.
edge_players.kills_it: The week he rushed for 52 shows the floor. It dies if Carolina's 37 percent blitz pulls Detroit into the 0.48-EPA pass script and Gibbs is the 52/61 rush-rec split, if Bartch's absence wrecks the run fits, or if a blowout pulls him after a slow start.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Gibbs lost because Carolina blitzed, Goff took the 0.48-EPA answers, Bartch's absence clogged the interior, and Gibbs finished on the 52-yard script while the bad run defense never got stressed — the 96.5 line was already his median, so the matchup upgrade was the whole bet and it never showed up. Hubbard lost because the game stayed close, Detroit's run defense (4.61 YPC, 12 explosive runs allowed) gave up one long carry, and 15-18 carries at even a modest yards per carry walked through 66.5 the way the 82-yard week already did; Lewis being out changed protection more than carry count. The slip lost together if Carolina controlled the line of scrimmage on both sides, which the missing spread cannot rule out.
slip_story: One story only: Detroit's offense is the better unit and Carolina cannot run. Stack is Gibbs rush-yards over with Hubbard rush-yards under (leader runs, trailer abandons the run, OL out on the trailer). Correlation is incomplete — if Detroit leads by passing against the blitz, Hubbard under can hit while Gibbs rush over misses — so this is a two-leg script slip, not a forced parlay. Do not add Carolina receiver overs, a game under, or a second market on either back. No touchdown legs. Weather and inactives can still break it.
